Added the implementation plan `blueprint/decompose-connect-error/` for decomposing the forward envelope's `CONNECT_ERROR` reason into evidence classes (`POOL_EXHAUSTED`, `TUNNEL_SETUP_FAILED`, `BACKEND_NOT_LISTENING`, plus a `detail` field describing the exception behind the failure), recording the cause on the minds health tracker, surfacing a device-side "this device cannot connect" verdict that outranks the restart episode's claims, evidence-gating the "Restarting" copy, and plumbing `was_host_started` through `mngr start` structured output. The plan also deletes the unconsumed recovery exec probe (`recovery_probe.py` machinery, the `/health` route, and the resolver-snapshot mirror), closing PR #305 as superseded. All of this ships as a single PR.

The plan folder also carries `verify_427_repro.py`, the manual-verification script for its own acceptance criterion: it drives a synthetic issue #427 (an SSH key with no known_hosts sibling) through the real forward app, the real consumer and tracker, the real recovery-info route, and a real render of the recovery card. It is a script rather than a test because it spans four layers the suite tests apart and shells out to the frontend toolchain.

The folder also carries `live-verification.md`, the record of driving the finished branch against a real docker workspace in the running desktop app: which classifications, verdicts, and copy were observed end to end, and the surfaces that still disagree.

`specs/allow-duplicate-agent-ids.md` is updated to match: the `resolver_snapshot` envelope it described as instance-keyed no longer exists, and its open item on that envelope's schema is settled by removal rather than by the migration it anticipated. The resolver's own service-map cache is untouched and still instance-keyed.
